executiveSummary: Catastrophic flash flooding in Nepal continues to drive the global risk picture, with authorities confirming 1,403 fatalities and 6,150 missing amid ongoing recovery operations at hydropower infrastructure. View Article Severe flash flooding across the Navajo Nation (U.S. Southwest) resulted in three deaths, evacuations, and road washouts isolating households and necessitating shelter and relief deliveries. View Article Monsoon flooding and landslides across northern and central Vietnam left at least four dead and inundated more than 16,000 homes; evacuations and transport disruption persist. View Article Typhoon-driven flooding in southeast China prompted mass movement, with nearly 600,000 people evacuated in Fujian amid widespread county-level impacts. View Article Hurricane Lowell caused major disruption in Hawaii, including blocked roads and roughly 30,000 power outages across islands, with localized evacuations reported. View Article Secondary but notable U.S. events include fatal flash flooding at the Grand Canyon (three deaths), regional water rescues and commuter disruption from mid-Atlantic/northeast floods, and California wildfire evacuations affecting ~900 residents. outlook72h: Nepal: Continued search and recovery with difficult terrain access; risk of localized slope instability near damaged hydropower works remains elevated. (Operational caution) Vietnam: Residual river flooding and sporadic landslides possible where soils are saturated; expect rolling transport disruption and debris management needs. (High uncertainty by micro-basin) Navajo Nation (U.S.): Short-notice flash flooding remains possible in storm-favored corridors; prioritize readiness for rapid road closures and shelter activation. (Readiness posture) Hawaii: Gradual utility restoration and debris clearance likely; watch for localized heavy showers complicating work zones. (Recovery operations) China (SE): Post-evacuation returns should be staged with floodplain safety checks and essential service verification. (Phased re-entry) Note: Outlook reflects seasonal patterns and current impact profiles; it is not a deterministic weather forecast.
regionalTrends: South and Southeast Asia: Late-monsoon flooding and landslides remain seasonally elevated, with saturated soils increasing secondary hazard risk (landslips, prolonged inundation).
Western Pacific: Typhoon-related coastal evacuations and riverine flooding are likely to recur, with rapid shifts in impact footprints across adjacent provinces.
U.S. Southwest and Intermountain West: Short-fuse flash flood risks persist where terrain funnels runoff (canyons, arroyos), amplifying life-safety concerns. Supporting Report
Hawaii and Central Pacific: Post-tropical recovery operations may be prolonged by debris clearance and utility restoration in affected islands. Source
U.S. West: Wildfire evacuations continue episodically where fuels and winds align; public land closures disrupt access and recreation. Source
